page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores. Cryptographic capabilities are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is exceptionally high, uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET throughput are highly competitive, positioning the instance well for memory-bound transactional workloads.

Conversely, the server shows limitations in heavy computational tasks like large-scale LLM text generation, where performance drops significantly. It maintains average throughput for static web serving, software compilation, and medium-model LLM prompt processing. This resource profile is highly cost-efficient for general-purpose enterprise applications, database hosting, and moderate parallel processing tasks that require dedicated AMD EPYC resources without the premium cost of specialized memory or GPU hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server configured with 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, running on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. Featuring 32 physical cores and multithreading, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU execution, excellent cryptographic processing, and high Redis database transaction speeds. However, uncached memory bandwidth and large-model language inference remain average to poor. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for enterprise workloads, database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring dedicated AMD EPYC resources.
